title: Transport of the Brown principle to independent universes
statement: Fix universes u, w, v, v_H and V=max(w,v,v_H). Let C have objects in Type u, morphisms in Type v, a triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category], Type V-indexed coproducts, and compact generators indexed in Type V [def-pc-compactly-generated]. If H:C^{op}→Ab_{v_H} [def-sp-abelian] is homological [def-sp-homological-functor] and preserves Type V-indexed products, then its underlying set-valued functor is representable: there exist G in C and bijections Hom_C(c,G)≃H(c), natural in c.

No extra common-universe Brown hypothesis is required.

lean.statement:
theorem brownCohomologicalRepresentabilityUniverseTransfer
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    [IsTriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{max w v vH} C]
    (hC : IsCompactlyGeneratedTriangulated.{max w v vH} C)
    (H : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{vH}) [H.IsHomological]
    (hH : ∀ I : Type (max w v vH), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) H) :
    (H ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat).IsRepresentable
